title: Fix broken Wi-Fi on 2015–2017 MacBook Pros by shipping the missing NVRAM file
author: csvenke
body:
## Issue

- 2015–2017 MacBook Pros (and any Apple machine with a BCM43602, PCI `14e4:43ba`/`43bb`/`43bc`) ship with `brcmfmac43602-pcie.bin` but **no board NVRAM** (`brcmfmac43602-pcie.txt`) — `linux-firmware` has never carried it.
- Without the NVRAM, the firmware's country detection breaks ([kernel bug 193121](https://bugzilla.kernel.org/show_bug.cgi?id=193121)): only 2.4 GHz networks appear, signal strength collapses, and the WPA 4-way handshake times out (`deauth reason=15`).
- `wpa_supplicant` misreports that timeout as *"pre-shared key may be incorrect"* and NetworkManager as *"psk mismatch"* — so affected users chase their passphrase instead of the real cause.
- This is a **second, distinct firmware defect** on the same chip as #6652. That quirk (`feature_disable=0x82000`) fixes the WPA-offload failure against WPA2/WPA3 transition APs; it was active on the machine below the whole time and was not sufficient. Both defects surface as "wrong password", which is why this one hides behind it.

## Fix

Vendor the known-good NVRAM (Apple Boot Camp driver lineage, from bug 193121) and install it for Apple machines carrying a BCM43602:

- `default/firmware/apple/brcmfmac43602-pcie.txt` — the NVRAM with `ccode=0`/`regrev=1`, which bypasses the broken country detection, plus a provenance header.
- `install/hardware/apple/fix-brcmfmac-nvram.sh` — install-time leaf, gated on Apple DMI vendor + `14e4:(43ba|43bb|43bc)` (narrower than the supplicant quirk's list: this NVRAM is 43602-family only, and BCM4360 Macs run the out-of-tree `wl` driver and are excluded for free). Substitutes the live interface MAC into the `macaddr=` line; strips it when no MAC is discoverable (the OTP fallback is proven). Never overwrites an existing file.
- `migrations/<epoch>.sh` — the same repair for existing installs: idempotent, env-overridable paths, never clobbers, sets `reboot-required` only when it actually installed — it does not reload `brcmfmac`, which would drop the Wi-Fi connection carrying the update.
- `test/shell.d/brcmfmac-nvram-test.sh` — 13 assertions covering gates, exclusions, MAC substitution/strip, idempotency, no-clobber, and the escalation contract.

## Evidence

MacBookPro14,3 (2017, BCM43602), before → after installing the NVRAM and reloading `brcmfmac`:

| | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| bands visible | 2.4 GHz only | 2.4 + 5 GHz |
| signal (same spot) | −92 dBm | −72 dBm |
| RX bitrate | 13 Mbit/s | 216 Mbit/s |
| WPA handshake | timeout, `reason=15` | completes in <1s |

Independent confirmations on 13,2 and 14,3: [mbp-2016-linux#172](https://github.com/Dunedan/mbp-2016-linux/issues/172), [mbp-2016-linux#208](https://github.com/Dunedan/mbp-2016-linux/issues/208).

## Provenance & licensing

The NVRAM is Broadcom-proprietary, extracted from Apple's Windows driver package — which is exactly why `linux-firmware` can't ship it and bug 193121 has been open for years. Vendoring it here is the same trade-off, made at the distro layer; if you'd rather not carry the file in-repo, the alternatives are fetch-at-install (the canonical bugzilla source is now behind an anti-bot wall, and the gists are a supply-chain risk) or detect-and-instruct (weak). Flagging it explicitly so the call is yours.

@@ -0,0 +1,268 @@
+# NVRAM for the Broadcom BCM43602 (PCI 14e4:43ba/43bb/43bc) in 2015-2017 Apple
+# Macs, extracted from Apple's Windows/Boot Camp driver package and surfaced via
+# kernel bug 193121, where it is attached as
+# https://bugzilla.kernel.org/attachment.cgi?id=285753. linux-firmware ships
+# only the .bin for this part, so without this file the firmware's country
+# detection never completes: scans come back 2.4GHz-only at crippled power and
+# the WPA four-way handshake times out.
+#
+# ccode=0/regrev=1 bypass that broken country detection by pinning the "world"
+# regulatory domain instead of asking the AP. The values below are otherwise the
+# board's own calibration data; do not edit them.
+#
+# Lines starting with # are comments to humans only; the brcmfmac NVRAM parser
+# ignores them.
+#
+# macaddr= below is the firmware's built-in fallback default (00:90:4c is the Epigram/Broadcom OUI, not a real
+# device MAC); the install leaf and migration always substitute the machine's live MAC or strip the line, so it is never used verbatim.
+boardrev=0x1101
+
+sromrev=11
+boardtype=0x073e
+vendid=0x14e4
+devid=0x43ba
+
+macaddr=00:90:4c:0d:f4:3e
+
+ccode=0
+regrev=1
+
+
+# Board flags:
+# X BFL_BTCOEXIST          = 0x00000001   This board implements Bluetooth coexistence
+#   BFL_EXTLNA             = 0x00001000   This board has an external LNA (2G)
+#   BFL_FEM_BT             = 0x00400000   This board has shared antenna w/ BT
+# X BFL_PALDO              = 0x02000000   Power topology uses PALDO ? - CHECK
+#   BFL_EXTLNA_5GHz        = 0x10000000   Board has an external LNA in 5GHz band
+boardflags=0x02000001
+
+# Board flags 2:
+#   BFL2_BT_SHARE_ANT0     = 0x00800000   share core0 antenna with BT
+# X BFL2_LNA1BYPFORTR2G    = 0x40000000   acphy, enable lna1 bypass for 2G clip lo
+# X BFL2_LNA1BYPFORTR5G    = 0x80000000   acphy, enable lna1 bypass for 5G clip lo
+# X BFL2_SPUR_WAR          = 0x00000200   Board has a WAR for clock-harmonic spurs
+#   BFL2_2G_SPUR_WAR       = 0x00002000   Board has a WAR to reduce and avoid clock-harmonic spurs in 2G band
+boardflags2=0xC0000000
+
+# Board flags 3:
+# X BFL3_RCAL_WAR          = 0x00000008   acphy rcal war active on this board (mainly for 4335a0)
+# X BFL3_FEMTBL_FROM_NVRAM = 0x00000100   acphy, femctrl table is read from nvram
+boardflags3=0x40000108
+
+#btc_mode=0

+#### added rx de-sense
+
+btcdyn_flags=0x7

+btcdyn_dflt_dsns_level=0

+btcdyn_msw_rows=1

+btcdyn_msw_row0=1,-16,-95,-100

+btcdyn_dsns_row0=4,-16,-63,-95

+#### end of rx de-sense

+

+########################################################
+# RF Control Definitions
+
+antswitch=0

+pa2ga0=-162,6368,-735

+cckbw202gpo=0x0000

@@ -0,0 +1,56 @@
+# 2015-2017 Apple Macs ship the Broadcom BCM43602, which brcmfmac drives. The
+# linux-firmware package provides only the .bin for this part and no NVRAM, and
+# without one the firmware's country-code detection never completes (kernel bug
+# 193121): scans come back 2.4GHz-only at a fraction of the real signal, and
+# the WPA four-way handshake times out, which NetworkManager reports as a
+# rejected password. Shipping the board's NVRAM with ccode=0/regrev=1 pins the
+# "world" regulatory domain around the broken detection and lets the handshake
+# complete. This pairs with fix-brcmfmac-supplicant.sh, which fixes a different
+# firmware defect on the same machines; neither replaces the other.
+#
+# The gate is deliberately narrower than the supplicant quirk's: the NVRAM
+# holds this board's calibration data, so it only applies to the BCM43602
+# family -- 14e4:43ba/43bb/43bc, the IDs brcmfmac's brcm_hw_ids.h lists for
+# BCM43602 and its single-band variants. BCM4360 (14e4:43a0) runs the
+# out-of-tree wl driver, which never reads brcmfmac NVRAM, and is excluded.
+#
+# A file already at the destination wins: user-placed or shipped by a future
+# linux-firmware, both outrank this copy, and the skip is silent because it is
+# the common case on reruns.
+#
+# The asset lives under default/, a sibling of the install tree, so it resolves
+# from $OMARCHY_PATH (exported by the install entry point and always present at
+# runtime) rather than from $OMARCHY_INSTALL, which points at install/ itself.
+dest=/usr/lib/firmware/brcm/brcmfmac43602-pcie.txt
+sys_vendor="$(cat /sys/class/dmi/id/sys_vendor 2>/dev/null || true)"
+
+if [[ ! -e $dest ]] && [[ $sys_vendor == Apple* ]] &&
+  lspci -nn | grep -E "14e4:(43ba|43bb|43bc)" >/dev/null; then
+  echo "Detected a Mac with BCM43602 Wi-Fi; installing its missing NVRAM"
+
+  # The NVRAM's macaddr= line carries the donor board's address, so substitute
+  # this NIC's own, found under the matching PCI device. lspci -D prints the
+  # domain form /sys uses. awk reads the whole stream instead of exiting on the
+  # first match, so the pipe stays safe under pipefail (#6608).
+  bdf="$(lspci -Dnn | awk '/14e4:(43ba|43bb|43bc)/ { if (!found) { print $1; found=1 } }')"
+  mac=""
+  if [[ -n $bdf ]]; then
+    net_addrs=(/sys/bus/pci/devices/"$bdf"/net/*/address)
+    mac="$(cat "${net_addrs[0]}" 2>/dev/null || true)"
+  fi
+
+  work="$(mktemp)"
+  if [[ -n $mac ]]; then
+    sed "s/^macaddr=.*/macaddr=$mac/" \
+      "$OMARCHY_PATH/default/firmware/apple/brcmfmac43602-pcie.txt" >"$work"
+  else
+    # No MAC discoverable: drop the line entirely and let the firmware fall
+    # back to the OTP address, which is how these NICs already run with no
+    # NVRAM at all.
+    sed '/^macaddr=/d' \
+      "$OMARCHY_PATH/default/firmware/apple/brcmfmac43602-pcie.txt" >"$work"
+  fi
+
+  install -Dm644 "$work" "$dest"
+  rm -f "$work"
+fi

@@ -0,0 +1,51 @@
+echo "Install the missing NVRAM for Broadcom BCM43602 Wi-Fi on Apple Macs"
+
+# The install-time leaf only reaches machines set up after it shipped, so an
+# existing install on a 2015-2017 Mac still has no NVRAM for its BCM43602:
+# 2.4GHz-only scans, crippled signal, and WPA handshakes that time out. See
+# install/hardware/apple/fix-brcmfmac-nvram.sh for the failure this fixes and
+# for why the gate is limited to 14e4:43ba/43bb/43bc.
+dmi_vendor="${OMARCHY_BRCMFMAC_NVRAM_DMI_VENDOR:-/sys/class/dmi/id/sys_vendor}"
+pci_devices="${OMARCHY_BRCMFMAC_NVRAM_PCI_DEVICES:-/sys/bus/pci/devices}"
+dest="${OMARCHY_BRCMFMAC_NVRAM_DEST:-/usr/lib/firmware/brcm/brcmfmac43602-pcie.txt}"
+src="${OMARCHY_BRCMFMAC_NVRAM_SRC:-$OMARCHY_PATH/default/firmware/apple/brcmfmac43602-pcie.txt}"
+
+sys_vendor="$(cat "$dmi_vendor" 2>/dev/null || true)"
+
+if ! [[ $sys_vendor == Apple* ]] ||
+  ! lspci -nn | grep -E "14e4:(43ba|43bb|43bc)" >/dev/null; then
+  exit 0
+fi
+
+# A file already there wins: user-placed or package-shipped, both outrank this
+# copy. The same check keeps the migration idempotent for the next user on a
+# machine already repaired.
+if [[ -e $dest ]]; then
+  exit 0
+fi
+
+# Substitute the NIC's live MAC for the donor board's placeholder, the same way
+# the install-time leaf does. awk reads the whole lspci stream instead of
+# exiting on the first match, so the pipe stays safe under pipefail (#6608).
+bdf="$(lspci -Dnn | awk '/14e4:(43ba|43bb|43bc)/ { if (!found) { print $1; found=1 } }')"
+mac=""
+if [[ -n $bdf ]]; then
+  net_addrs=("$pci_devices/$bdf"/net/*/address)
+  mac="$(cat "${net_addrs[0]}" 2>/dev/null || true)"
+fi
+
+work="$(mktemp)"
+if [[ -n $mac ]]; then
+  sed "s/^macaddr=.*/macaddr=$mac/" "$src" >"$work"
+else
+  # No MAC discoverable: drop the line and let the firmware use the OTP
+  # address, which is how these NICs already run with no NVRAM at all.
+  sed '/^macaddr=/d' "$src" >"$work"
+fi
+
+sudo install -Dm644 "$work" "$dest"
+rm -f "$work"
+
+# brcmfmac reads the NVRAM when the module loads. Reloading it here would drop
+# the user's live Wi-Fi connection, possibly the one carrying this update.
+omarchy-state set reboot-required

@@ -0,0 +1,235 @@
+#!/bin/bash
+
+set -euo pipefail
+
+source "$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)/base-test.sh"
+
+leaf="$ROOT/install/hardware/apple/fix-brcmfmac-nvram.sh"
+all="$ROOT/install/hardware/all.sh"
+asset="$ROOT/default/firmware/apple/brcmfmac43602-pcie.txt"
+migration="$ROOT/migrations/1786961462.sh"
+
+grep -q 'apple/fix-brcmfmac-nvram.sh' "$all" ||
+  fail "the BCM43602 NVRAM leaf runs during hardware setup"
+pass "the BCM43602 NVRAM leaf runs during hardware setup"
+
+# The vendored NVRAM is the fix: ccode=0/regrev=1 pin the "world" regulatory
+# domain around the firmware's broken country detection (kernel bug 193121).
+grep -qx 'ccode=0' "$asset" || fail "the vendored NVRAM keeps ccode=0"
+grep -qx 'regrev=1' "$asset" || fail "the vendored NVRAM keeps regrev=1"
+grep -q '^macaddr=' "$asset" ||
+  fail "the vendored NVRAM carries a macaddr placeholder to substitute"
+grep -q '193121' "$asset" || fail "the vendored NVRAM documents its provenance"
+grep -qF 'https://bugzilla.kernel.org/attachment.cgi?id=285753' "$asset" ||
+  fail "the vendored NVRAM names the exact attachment it was vendored from"
+pass "the vendored NVRAM keeps ccode=0/regrev=1 and documents its provenance"
+
+test_tmp=$(mktemp -d)
+trap 'rm -rf "$test_tmp"' EXIT
+
+stub_bin="$test_tmp/bin"
+calls="$test_tmp/calls.log"
+dest="$test_tmp/firmware/brcm/brcmfmac43602-pcie.txt"
+pci_devices="$test_tmp/sys-pci"
+mkdir -p "$stub_bin" "$test_tmp/dmi"
+
+cat >"$stub_bin/lspci" <<'SH'
+#!/bin/bash
+
+# Real lspci prints the domain in the BDF only when -D is passed, and /sys uses
+# the domain form, so a consumer regressed to parsing plain lspci -nn output
+# finds no MAC here and the tests that expect one fail loudly.
+domain=0
+for arg in "$@"; do
+  if [[ $arg == -*D* ]]; then
+    domain=1
+  fi
+done
+
+if (( domain == 1 )); then
+  wifi_bdf=0000:03:00.0
+  filler_bdf=0000:02:00.0
+else
+  wifi_bdf=03:00.0
+  filler_bdf=02:00.0
+fi
+
+# Chatty like real lspci: keep writing well past the pipe buffer after the
+# match, so a partially-read pipe would kill this stub with SIGPIPE and
+# pipefail would read that as "no such hardware" (#6608).
+if [[ -n ${WIFI_ID:-} ]]; then
+  echo "$wifi_bdf Network controller [0280]: Broadcom Inc. Wireless [14e4:$WIFI_ID]"
+fi
+for _ in {1..4096}; do
+  echo "$filler_bdf Host bridge [0600]: Filler Device [ffff:0000]"
+done
+SH
+
+cat >"$stub_bin/sudo" <<'SH'
+#!/bin/bash
+
+printf 'sudo' >>"$TEST_LOG"
+printf '\t%s' "$@" >>"$TEST_LOG"
+printf '\n' >>"$TEST_LOG"
+"$@"
+SH
+
+# Stubbed rather than run: the real one would write the running user's state.
+cat >"$stub_bin/omarchy-state" <<'SH'
+#!/bin/bash
+
+printf 'omarchy-state' >>"$TEST_LOG"
+printf '\t%s' "$@" >>"$TEST_LOG"
+printf '\n' >>"$TEST_LOG"
+SH
+
+chmod +x "$stub_bin"/*
+
+# The NIC's live address, exposed the way /sys does: under the PCI device's
+# net/ directory, named for the bdf the lspci stub reports.
+provide_mac() {
+  mkdir -p "$pci_devices/0000:03:00.0/net/wlp3s0"
+  printf 'aa:bb:cc:dd:ee:ff\n' >"$pci_devices/0000:03:00.0/net/wlp3s0/address"
+}
+
+# The leaf reads absolute paths, so redirect them into the sandbox with sed and
+# point OMARCHY_PATH at the real tree for the vendored asset. pipefail is on,
+# so a partially-read lspci pipe would go silent here the way #6608 did.
+run_leaf() {
+  local vendor="$1" wifi_id="${2:-}"
+  printf '%s' "$vendor" >"$test_tmp/dmi/sys_vendor"
+
+  local script="$test_tmp/leaf.sh"
+  sed -e "s|/sys/class/dmi/id/sys_vendor|$test_tmp/dmi/sys_vendor|g" \
+      -e "s|/usr/lib/firmware/brcm|$test_tmp/firmware/brcm|g" \
+      -e "s|/sys/bus/pci/devices|$pci_devices|g" \
+      "$leaf" >"$script"
+
+  WIFI_ID="$wifi_id" PATH="$stub_bin:$PATH" OMARCHY_PATH="$ROOT" \
+    bash -eE -o pipefail -c 'source "$1"' bash "$script" </dev/null
+}
+
+# BCM43602 and its single-band variants, on a Mac with no T2 to detect.
+for wifi_id in 43ba 43bb 43bc; do
+  rm -rf "$test_tmp/firmware" "$pci_devices"
+  provide_mac
+  run_leaf "Apple Inc." "$wifi_id" >/dev/null
+  [[ -f $dest ]] || fail "a Mac with 14e4:$wifi_id gets the NVRAM"
+  [[ $(stat -c %a "$dest") == "644" ]] ||
+    fail "the NVRAM installs world-readable" "14e4:$wifi_id: $(stat -c %a "$dest")"
+  grep -qx 'ccode=0' "$dest" || fail "the installed NVRAM keeps ccode=0" "14e4:$wifi_id"
+  grep -qx 'regrev=1' "$dest" || fail "the installed NVRAM keeps regrev=1" "14e4:$wifi_id"
+  grep -qx 'macaddr=aa:bb:cc:dd:ee:ff' "$dest" ||
+    fail "the installed NVRAM carries the NIC's live MAC" "14e4:$wifi_id: $(grep '^macaddr' "$dest")"
+done
+pass "every BCM43602 part gets the NVRAM with its live MAC substituted"
+
+# Older Macs report the vendor differently.
+rm -rf "$test_tmp/firmware" "$pci_devices"
+provide_mac
+run_leaf "Apple Computer, Inc." 43ba >/dev/null
+[[ -f $dest ]] || fail "the older Apple vendor string is recognized"
+pass "the older Apple vendor string is recognized"
+
+# With no MAC discoverable the line goes away entirely; the firmware falls back
+# to the OTP address, which is how these NICs already run with no NVRAM.
+rm -rf "$test_tmp/firmware" "$pci_devices"
+run_leaf "Apple Inc." 43ba >/dev/null
+[[ -f $dest ]] || fail "a Mac with no discoverable MAC still gets the NVRAM"
+! grep -q '^macaddr=' "$dest" ||
+  fail "the macaddr line is stripped when no MAC is discoverable" "$(grep '^macaddr' "$dest")"
+grep -qx 'ccode=0' "$dest" || fail "the installed NVRAM keeps ccode=0"
+pass "the macaddr line is stripped when no MAC is discoverable"
+
+# BCM4360 Macs run the out-of-tree wl driver, which never reads this file, so
+# installing it would only look like the machine had been dealt with.
+rm -rf "$test_tmp/firmware" "$pci_devices"
+run_leaf "Apple Inc." 43a0 >/dev/null
+[[ ! -e $dest ]] || fail "a Mac whose Wi-Fi the wl driver drives is left alone"
+pass "a Mac whose Wi-Fi the wl driver drives is left alone"
+
+# Plenty of non-Apple hardware uses brcmfmac and does not share this bug.
+rm -rf "$test_tmp/firmware"
+run_leaf "LENOVO" 43ba >/dev/null
+[[ ! -e $dest ]] || fail "non-Apple hardware is left alone"
+pass "non-Apple hardware is left alone"
+
+# An iMac on Ethernet alone has no 14e4 device for the gate to match at all.
+run_leaf "Apple Inc." "" >/dev/null
+[[ ! -e $dest ]] || fail "a Mac with no wireless device is left alone"
+pass "a Mac with no wireless device is left alone"
+
+# An existing file wins, user-placed or package-shipped.
+rm -rf "$test_tmp/firmware" "$pci_devices"
+provide_mac
+mkdir -p "$(dirname "$dest")"
+printf 'user-owned\n' >"$dest"
+run_leaf "Apple Inc." 43ba >/dev/null
+grep -qx 'user-owned' "$dest" ||
+  fail "an existing NVRAM is never clobbered" "$(cat "$dest")"
+pass "an existing NVRAM is never clobbered"
+
+# Installs that predate the leaf never ran it, so the migration has to reach
+# them. It runs as the user under pipefail, the context #6608 was about.
+run_migration() {
+  local vendor="$1" wifi_id="${2:-}"
+  printf '%s' "$vendor" >"$test_tmp/dmi/sys_vendor"
+  : >"$calls"
+
+  WIFI_ID="$wifi_id" PATH="$stub_bin:$PATH" TEST_LOG="$calls" OMARCHY_PATH="$ROOT" \
+    OMARCHY_BRCMFMAC_NVRAM_DMI_VENDOR="$test_tmp/dmi/sys_vendor" \
+    OMARCHY_BRCMFMAC_NVRAM_PCI_DEVICES="$pci_devices" \
+    OMARCHY_BRCMFMAC_NVRAM_DEST="$dest" \
+    bash -euo pipefail "$migration" >/dev/null
+}
+
+# The machine this was written for: a Mac with a BCM43602 and no NVRAM.
+rm -rf "$test_tmp/firmware" "$pci_devices"
+provide_mac
+run_migration "Apple Inc." 43ba
+grep -qx 'ccode=0' "$dest" 2>/dev/null ||
+  fail "the migration installs the NVRAM" "$(ls -R "$test_tmp/firmware" 2>&1)"
+grep -qx 'macaddr=aa:bb:cc:dd:ee:ff' "$dest" ||
+  fail "the migration substitutes the live MAC" "$(grep '^macaddr' "$dest")"
+# The NVRAM only reaches the firmware when brcmfmac next loads.
+grep -Fq $'omarchy-state\tset\treboot-required' "$calls" ||
+  fail "the migration asks for the reboot that applies it" "$(cat "$calls")"
+pass "the migration installs the NVRAM and asks for a reboot"
+
+run_migration "Apple Inc." 43ba
+[[ ! -s $calls ]] || fail "a repaired install is left untouched" "$(cat "$calls")"
+pass "the migration is idempotent"
+
+# No sysfs address for the NIC: the macaddr line is stripped rather than left
+# as the donor board's, and the reboot is still requested.
+rm -rf "$test_tmp/firmware" "$pci_devices"
+run_migration "Apple Inc." 43ba
+[[ -f $dest ]] ||
+  fail "the migration installs the NVRAM without a discoverable MAC" "$(ls -R "$test_tmp/firmware" 2>&1)"
+! grep -q '^macaddr=' "$dest" ||
+  fail "the migration strips macaddr when no MAC is discoverable" "$(grep '^macaddr' "$dest")"
+grep -Fq $'omarchy-state\tset\treboot-required' "$calls" ||
+  fail "the migration still asks for the reboot that applies it" "$(cat "$calls")"
+pass "the migration strips macaddr when no MAC is discoverable and still asks for a reboot"
+
+# A file that appeared between leaf and migration -- package update or user --
+# outranks the vendored copy.
+rm -rf "$test_tmp/firmware"
+mkdir -p "$(dirname "$dest")"
+printf 'package-shipped\n' >"$dest"
+run_migration "Apple Inc." 43ba
+grep -qx 'package-shipped' "$dest" ||
+  fail "the migration never overwrites an existing NVRAM" "$(cat "$dest")"
+[[ ! -s $calls ]] || fail "the migration escalates nothing when the file already exists" "$(cat "$calls")"
+pass "the migration never overwrites an existing NVRAM"
+
+rm -rf "$test_tmp/firmware"
+run_migration "Apple Inc." 43a0
+[[ ! -e $dest ]] || fail "the migration skips a Mac the wl driver drives"
+[[ ! -s $calls ]] || fail "the migration escalates nothing on unaffected Macs" "$(cat "$calls")"
+pass "the migration skips hardware the NVRAM does not describe"
+
+run_migration "LENOVO" 43ba
+[[ ! -e $dest ]] || fail "the migration skips non-Apple hardware"
+[[ ! -s $calls ]] || fail "the migration escalates nothing on non-Apple hardware" "$(cat "$calls")"
+pass "the migration skips non-Apple hardware"

comments.body:
Can confirm this fixes it on a MacBookPro14,3 (15" 2017 Touch Bar, BCM43602 14e4:43ba, Omarchy 4.0.1, kernel 7.1.9-arch1-2). Out of the box I had exactly the symptoms described here: no `clm_blob` available in `dmesg` on every boot, only 2.4GHz networks visible, terrible signal. In a room with weak coverage the scan list was completely empty, which first sent me down the `broadcom-wl-dkms` rabbit hole (wrong driver for this chip, and it blacklists `brcmfmac` — don't).

Installed the NVRAM file from this PR into `/usr/lib/firmware/brcm/`, reloaded the driver, and the 5GHz band appeared (channels 36–165, VHT80). Getting 160+ Mbps near the router now. I'm in Germany, so ccode=0 also works fine in an ETSI regulatory domain.

Two small notes:
  - Testing without a reboot: `modprobe -r brcmfmac` fails with "module in use" until you remove `brcmfmac_wcc` first. The migration's reboot-required approach avoids this.
  - The file declares 2 antenna chains, but the 15" board is 3x3 (HT MCS caps at 0–15 instead of 0–23). Still a massive improvement over no 5GHz at all.

Reviewed on a disposable worker VM, with an independent second opinion from Codex at xhigh reasoning. Three things still need a decision from you or from the maintainer, and the confirmation report above — welcome as it is — does not settle any of them.

### Tests

`test/shell.d/brcmfmac-nvram-test.sh` (15 assertions) and `./test/cli` (116 assertions) both pass on the worker. Nothing was exercised on real hardware: the coordinator has no BCM43602, so everything below is read out of the source and the vendored file rather than measured on a Mac.

### Still open

**1. The destination sits inside linux-firmware's own directory.** `install/hardware/apple/fix-brcmfmac-nvram.sh:24` and `migrations/1786961462.sh:10` write `/usr/lib/firmware/brcm/brcmfmac43602-pcie.txt`, a path no package owns. The day `linux-firmware-broadcom` ships that filename, pacman refuses the upgrade for everyone who ran this. `test/shell.d/unowned-system-paths-test.sh` exists to catch exactly that, and it passes green on this branch: it reads the destination off the command, and here the destination is held in `$dest` — the escape hatch its own header documents at line 11. `/usr/lib/firmware/updates/brcm/` is the kernel's override directory, searched ahead of `/usr/lib/firmware`, and installing there gets the same effect with no future conflict.

**2. One board's calibration is installed on boards that are not that board.** The vendored file declares `devid=0x43ba`, `boardtype=0x073e`, `boardrev=0x1101` and `rxchain=3`/`txchain=3`/`aa2g=3`/`aa5g=3`, and the gate at `fix-brcmfmac-nvram.sh:27` installs it byte-identically on `43bb` and `43bc` too. `brcmfmac-nvram-test.sh:113` loops `for wifi_id in 43ba 43bb 43bc` and asserts all three receive the same file, so the suite pins this as intended behaviour rather than catching it. The antenna note in the report above is this same defect seen from the other end: `3` is the bitmask `0b011`, two chains, so on a 3x3 board the file caps HT at MCS 15 instead of 23 — measurable underperformance on a `43ba` machine the file otherwise works on. A confirmation on one MacBookPro14,3 cannot speak for the single-band variants, and those are where the exposure is largest, because nobody reporting here has one.

**3. The MAC baked into the NVRAM may be a temporary one.** `fix-brcmfmac-nvram.sh:35` and `1786961462.sh:30` read `/sys/bus/pci/devices/<bdf>/net/*/address`, which under NetworkManager's default scan randomisation is a random locally-administered address whenever the interface is unassociated — and it is then written permanently into firmware NVRAM. Nothing in the repo overrides that default. `perm_address`, beside it in the same directory, is the permanent address and is the usual source for this; it reads all-zero on some drivers, so falling back to `address` when it does would be the complete form.

### On the confirmation report

Thank you for it — before-and-after on real hardware is the part nobody else can supply, and the `broadcom-wl-dkms` warning will save the next person an evening. Both of your notes, answered. The `brcmfmac_wcc` unload order is a testing detail rather than a defect here: the migration deliberately does not reload the module (`1786961462.sh:49`) and sets `reboot-required` instead, so nobody following the shipped path hits it. And `ccode=0` behaving well in an ETSI domain is a genuine data point but not a general regulatory clearance — it shows channels appearing and throughput arriving, not per-channel no-IR/DFS state or EIRP limits. Omarchy does persist a country from the timezone in `install/hardware/set-wireless-regdom.sh`, and brcmfmac forwards a non-world cfg80211 country through to the firmware, so the pinned `ccode=0`/`regrev=1` acts as a fallback rather than the last word — worth saying out loud, since the PR does not currently rest on it.

### Second opinion

Codex at xhigh reasoning agreed that all three findings remain open and that a single field report answers none of them; its independence is not currently guaranteed, since it can read this session's own working files, so read that as agreement rather than a separate discovery. It did contribute two things this review had not reasoned out: the arithmetic behind the antenna point — that `3` and `7` are bitmasks of enabled RF paths, and that Linux treats HT MCS 8-15 as two-stream and 16-23 as three-stream — and the argument that the observation belongs inside finding 2 rather than beside it as a fourth, since the root defect in both is one board dump generalised to hardware with a different RF topology. It also found the `set-wireless-regdom.sh` mitigation noted above.

### Where this stands

Waiting on both of us. The maintainer has a call no amount of review settles: whether Omarchy vendors a Broadcom-proprietary blob at all. You flagged that yourself in the description and were right to. Waiting on you are findings 1 and 2 — the destination path, and either narrowing the gate to `43ba` or shipping per-variant data — and finding 3, which is close to a one-line change. Nothing was pushed to your branch: the choice inside finding 2 is about hardware you have and this reviewer does not, and it is yours to make rather than to receive as a commit.

PR #7671 is an open, competing implementation of the same fix, built on a different NVRAM dump. Choosing between the two, or asking for one merged approach, is the maintainer's call; there is nothing here for you to act on.

A/B test on MacBookPro11,5 (BCM43602 14e4:43ba, same chip, different board): baseline has no NVRAM (no clm_blob in journal) yet 5GHz already works here (5180MHz, -30dBm, 400/400Mbit/s, 14x5GHz nets visible), so this tests cross-board safety, not efficacy.

Ran the actual leaf: installs a 7131-byte file with macaddr correctly substituted for this NIC's real (non-random) address. Reload recipe that works: nmcli disconnect + ip link down + modprobe -r brcmfmac_wcc, then brcmfmac (wcc must go first; plain modprobe -r brcmfmac fails 'in use'). Note reconnect needs explicit nmcli dev connect -- disconnect blocks autoconnect by design.

With NVRAM loaded: identical link (5180, 400/400), scans no worse (20x5GHz, within rescan variance), clm_blob still absent (expected -- NVRAM is not CLM). Reverted afterwards; baseline restored exactly. No degradation on this 3x3 board -- with one caveat: at VHT 400Mbit/s the HT MCS-cap concern from review is not exercised, so this does not settle that half of the cross-board question, only that nothing regresses at these rates.

One correction to the thread discussion: /sys/class/net/wlp4s0/perm_address does not exist at all on brcmfmac here (not all-zero, absent), so a perm_address-first fallback would need to handle ENOENT, not just zero content -- and would land back on address anyway, which is what the leaf already reads.

Addendum -- HT/VHT capability check for the cross-board question, same MacBookPro11,5. With the NVRAM loaded and the driver reloaded, iw phy advertises byte-identical capabilities to baseline: HT MCS 0-23 and VHT MCS 0-9 on all 3 streams, link still 400/400. So the file's rxchain/txchain=3 mask does not shrink the advertised stream support on this 3x3 board -- the predicted MCS cap does not materialize at the advertisement level. Caveat: advertisement is not runtime enforcement; forcing HT MCS 16-23 would be the final proof, but that needs a 3SS AP and band manipulation, and with identical advertisements plus identical link rates there is no signal pointing at hidden harm.

Another MacBookPro14,3 data point, and one result that bears on the cross-board question @rand0mdud3 raised. First, confirming @bernardcosta: this PR's file does fix 5 GHz here. MacBookPro14,3 (15-inch 2017, T1), Omarchy 4.0.3, kernel 7.2.3-arch1-3, BCM43602 `14e4:43ba`, Apple subsystem `106b:0173`. Stock install sees no 5 GHz band at all (`iw phy` has no Band 2); with the file installed, 29 channels appear and the machine associates on 5240 MHz. **On this board the file does halve advertised spatial streams.** @rand0mdud3's MacBookPro11,5 result was that `rxchain/txchain=3` left capabilities byte-identical to baseline — HT MCS 0-23 and VHT MCS 0-9 on all three streams. That does not reproduce here. Swapping between this PR's attachment 285753 and #7671's attachment 290569 on the same machine, same session, changes what the driver advertises: | | 290569 (`boardtype=0x61b`, `txchain=7`) | 285753 (`boardtype=0x073e`, `txchain=3`) | |---|---|---| | HT MCS | 0-23 | 0-15 | | VHT caps | `0x0c025820` | `0x0c015820` | | VHT RX/TX streams | 3 | 2 |
Raw iw phy info, Band 2, both calibrations ``` ===== 290569 (PR #7671) ===== aa2g=7 aa5g=7 boardrev=0x1421 boardtype=0x61b ccode=00 regrev=245 rxchain=7 txchain=7 HT TX/RX MCS rate indexes supported: 0-23 VHT Capabilities (0x0c025820): VHT RX MCS set: 1 streams: MCS 0-9 2 streams: MCS 0-9 3 streams: MCS 0-9 4 streams: not supported VHT TX MCS set: 1 streams: MCS 0-9 2 streams: MCS 0-9 3 streams: MCS 0-9 4 streams: not supported ===== 285753 (this PR) ===== aa2g=3 aa5g=3 boardrev=0x1101 boardtype=0x073e ccode=0 regrev=1 rxchain=3 txchain=3 HT TX/RX MCS rate indexes supported: 0-15 VHT Capabilities (0x0c015820): VHT RX MCS set: 1 streams: MCS 0-9 2 streams: MCS 0-9 3 streams: not supported VHT TX MCS set: 1 streams: MCS 0-9 2 streams: MCS 0-9 3 streams: not supported ```
So the effect looks board-dependent rather than absent: the 11,5 board keeps its three streams under this mask, the 14,3 board does not. Worth noting since #7671 gates specifically on 14,2/14,3. **Signal readings are not comparable between the two files.** The RSSI offset is itself calibration data, and the difference here is large and reproducible — 14.5 dB on an unchanged machine, position and AP: ``` 290569 (run 1): -63.8 dBm (mean of 5) 285753: -78.4 dBm 290569 (run 2): -64.0 dBm ``` I mention it because "signal got worse" is an easy and wrong conclusion to draw when comparing these two files; the word `rssi` does not appear anywhere in this thread or #7671. **Throughput did not separate them, and I would not trust anyone's single-pass numbers here, including my own earlier ones.** A/B/A, three 50 MB downloads per phase: ``` 290569 (run 1): 71.4 78.3 77.7 -> 75.8 Mbit/s 285753: 78.8 79.0 83.1 -> 80.3 Mbit/s 290569 (run 2): 66.8 64.6 48.9 -> 60.1 Mbit/s ``` The spread between the two identical control runs (15.7 Mbit/s) is over three times the A-vs-B difference (4.5 Mbit/s), so this environment cannot resolve it. One caveat that probably caps both: my AP advertises `VHT operation: channel width 1, center freq segment 1: 42, segment 2: 50`, i.e. 160 MHz, which this card does not support (`Supported Channel Width: neither 160 nor 80+80`). The link falls back to HT40 rates on both files, so neither calibration is being exercised near its ceiling. Someone with an 80 MHz AP would get a more meaningful comparison.

Measured data from a `106b:015a` board (MacBookPro13,3), in case it is useful here.

This NVRAM file is from subsystem **`106b:0157`**. On `106b:015a` it does enable 5 GHz — and it also stops 2.4 GHz from associating. The responsible key is a single one: **`sromrev=11`**. It does not *add* 5 GHz, it *switches* which band works, by activating the foreign board's srom11 calibration set.

Measured in both directions, after a full reboot each time (`modprobe -r brcmfmac_wcc` segfaults on this kernel, so reloads were avoided):

| NVRAM | 2.4 GHz | 5 GHz |
|---|---|---|
| full `0157` file, 144 keys | `CTRL-EVENT-ASSOC-REJECT status_code=16`, **zero entries AP-side** | associates |
| same file **minus `sromrev` only** (one line) | `CTRL-EVENT-CONNECTED`, **AP registration table gains the station** | does not associate |
| no file | associates | 0 channels offered |

The falsifier throughout was the **AP-side registration table**, not the client's own status. `nmcli` is unusable as an instrument here: it returns `Secrets were required, but not provided` from its own secrets layer *before* any frame reaches the radio, which reads exactly like a radio failure. Association was driven by `wpa_supplicant` with NetworkManager off the interface.

**`boardrev` is excluded with its real value, not merely by removal.** macOS on the same machine reports via `IO80211HardwareVersion`:

```
boardid: 0x15a   boardvendor: 0x106b   boardrev: 0x1108
```

The file declares `boardrev=0x1101`. Setting it to the measured `0x1108` — one changed line — did **not** restore 2.4 GHz (same `status_code=16`, same zero entries AP-side), while 5 GHz kept associating.

Two further measured facts:

- With no CLM blob the card does not see DFS channels at all. An AP on 5500 MHz was invisible at 23 dBm; the same AP on 5180 MHz appeared immediately. Any 5 GHz AP for these machines has to be on ch 36–48.
- Apple EFI passes **no** device properties to this PCI device: with `dump_apple_properties` and `log_buf_len=32M`, 91 devices were dumped and `0000:03:00.0` received zero. macOS IORegistry contains no `wifi-calibration-msf` or `wifi-antenna-sku-info` either. OTP on this card reads blank.

I am not proposing a fix and not asserting a cause beyond the table above. Whether correct srom11 data for `106b:015a` exists in retrievable form is unknown to me — the three sources I could measure were all empty.

@gunars — a third board, and on this one `sromrev=11` does not switch bands.

MacBookPro14,3, Apple subsystem `106b:0173` (same machine as my earlier comment, now on kernel 7.2.5-3-omarchy). This PR's file unmodified, 147 keys, `sromrev=11` present; identified by the same keys as before, `boardrev=0x1101` / `boardtype=0x073e` / `txchain=3`. Both bands work at the same time:

| | result |
|---|---|
| 2.4 GHz | associates — `CTRL-EVENT-CONNECTED`, 2457 MHz (ch 10), NetworkManager then completes activation |
| 5 GHz | associates, 5240 MHz, as reported earlier |
| phy channel list | 14 on 2.4 GHz, 29 on 5 GHz |

So the three boards in this thread now read: the file originates from `106b:0157`, your `106b:015a` loses 2.4 GHz with it, this `106b:0173` keeps it. That is the same shape as the other divergence here — the halved stream count I measured on this board did not reproduce on @rand0mdud3's 11,5 board either. Board-dependent rather than absent, in both cases.

**On your instrument warning.** Agreed that nmcli is not evidence, and I did not rely on it — but my falsifier is weaker than yours and I want that on the record. I do not control this AP, so I have no registration table. What I have is the supplicant's own `CTRL-EVENT-CONNECTED`, i.e. the 4-way handshake completed, which the AP cannot complete without accepting the station. Association was driven through NetworkManager; the evidence is taken from `wpa_supplicant`, not from NM's return code.

**DFS: I can neither confirm nor refute.** There is no AP on a DFS channel here to test against. For what it is worth, on this board those channels are present in the phy list rather than missing:

```
* 5260 MHz [52]  ... No IR | Radar detection | DFS state: usable (for 734 sec) | DFS CAC time: 60000 ms
  ... through ...
* 5720 MHz [144] ... No IR | Radar detection | DFS state: usable (for 734 sec) | DFS CAC time: 60000 ms
```

`no clm_blob available (err=-2)` is logged here too. So if these cards cannot hear DFS beacons without a CLM blob, on this board at least the mechanism is not cfg80211 dropping the channels.

**One methodology note that may save you reboots.** You avoided module reloads because `modprobe -r brcmfmac_wcc` segfaults on your kernel. On 7.2.5-3-omarchy the reload is clean:

```
modprobe -r brcmfmac_wcc && modprobe -r brcmfmac && modprobe brcmfmac
```

The interface returns and reassociates in 7 seconds, with nothing in dmesg beyond the expected `bus is down` during teardown and a normal firmware reload. Different kernel from yours, so this is a data point rather than a contradiction.

Fourth board for the matrix: MacBookPro11,5, Apple subsystem 106b:0152 (BCM43602 14e4:43ba). Both bands work with and without the file here (associated 5180 MHz, 12+ 5GHz nets visible stock), and with the file loaded the advertised caps stayed byte-identical (HT 0-23, VHT 3x0-9) with unchanged link rates -- so 0152 neither needs the file nor is harmed by it at VHT rates.
